## Status and use

This is the design data dictionary for the first registry release. **Core** fields are required for safe workflow, denominator management and M01--M26 reporting. **Extended** fields may be added later or hidden in the initial REDCap build. **Derived** fields are calculated in REDCap or the analysis pipeline and should not be manually entered.

Dates are collected as `date_dmy`. Repeating instruments use the REDCap repeat instance as their operational row identifier; a separate typed event ID is optional and not required for analysis.

## Shared reporting metric codebook

| Codes | Purpose |
|---|---|
| M01--M06 | Diabetes burden and descriptive measures |
| M07--M19 | Care processes, clinical control, prevention and treatment measures |
| M20 | Diagnosis-confirmation quality |
| M21--M26 | Review coverage and delivery of the structured care pathway |

## Table 2. Contact, residence, vital status and follow-up history — repeating restricted record

| Variable | Meaning / values | Status | Metrics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_status_date` | Date this contact, residence, vital-status or follow-up record became effective | Core | Denominator and history selection |
| `internal_redcap_id` | Registry record key | Core | Linkage |
| `first_name`, `family_name`, `middle_name`, `previous_name` | Identifying or matching names | Core; Core; Extended; Extended | Recall/linkage |
| `phone_1`, `phone_2`, `phone_3`, `email` | Contact details | Core; Extended; Extended; Extended | Recall |
| `preferred_contact_method` | Phone; SMS; email; letter; family contact; community visit; other | Core | Recall |
| `contact_permission_status` | Allowed; restricted; declined; unable to confirm | Core | Recall |
| `usual_st_helena_address` | Address or district applying from `contact_status_date`; later records preserve prior addresses | Core | Residence/recall |
| `nominated_contact` | Contact person, relationship and contact details | Extended | Recall |
| `residence_status` | Resident in St Helena; temporarily overseas for employment; temporarily overseas for medical care; temporarily overseas for other reason; permanently left/settled overseas; unknown | Core | M01, M02, M20--M26 |
| `expected_return_date` | Expected return to St Helena, where known | Core when temporarily overseas | Recall/denominator reconciliation |
| `vital_status` | Alive; deceased; unknown | Core | All denominators |
| `date_of_death` | Date of death | Core when deceased | All denominators |
| `date_last_diabetes_review` | Most recent completed diabetes-team consultation/review at this status record | Derived | M21, M22 |
| `next_review_due_date` | Date next six-monthly diabetes-team review is due | Derived | M21, M22 |
| `missed_six_month_review_count` | Consecutive scheduled six-monthly reviews missed | Derived | M21, M22 |
| `follow_up_status` | Up to date; potentially defaulted; definitely defaulted; re-engaged; follow-up temporarily suspended; unknown | Core | M21, M22 and active-register derivation |
| `follow_up_status_date` | Date the current follow-up status was assigned | Core | M21, M22 |
| `follow_up_reason` | Temporary overseas employment; temporary overseas medical care; transfer to another provider; permanently left/settled overseas; unable to contact; declined/no longer wishes follow-up; illness/disability; other; unknown | Core when follow-up is not up to date | Recall, M21, M22 |
| `follow_up_reason_other` | Free-text explanation where `follow_up_reason = other` | Core when other | Recall/data quality |
| `active_follow_up_flag` | Derived: eligible for routine local diabetes-team monitoring and re-engagement, yes/no; includes potentially and definitely defaulted residents | Derived | M20--M26 |
| `last_status_review_date` | Date contact, residence, vital status and follow-up status were last reviewed | Core | Denominator quality |

The latest Table 2 record on or before the reporting date defines current contact, residence, vital and follow-up status. Earlier repeat instances retain address, migration and follow-up history. A default category is never used to represent known migration, medical travel, transfer of care or death.

### Follow-up status operational rule

For the routine six-monthly pathway, `potentially defaulted` means one scheduled review was not completed within 30 days after its due date. `Definitely defaulted` means two consecutive scheduled reviews were not completed, normally at least 12 months after the last completed diabetes-team review, and at least one contact/tracing attempt has been documented. A completed later review changes the current status to `re-engaged`; the preceding repeat instance remains part of the history.

## Build rules

- REDCap user rights must restrict Table 2 to staff who require identifiers for recall and record resolution.
- Configure Table 2 as a repeating instrument. Create a new repeat instance whenever material contact, address, residence, vital or follow-up status changes; do not overwrite a previous status episode.
- Record data-quality queries rather than overwriting uncertain results or classifications without an audit trail.
- Do not store a static current age; derive age against the reporting date.
- Do not add clinical reference-range flags until ranges, units, and clinical responsibility have been agreed locally.
- The Statistical Analysis Plan, rather than calculated fields alone, is the authoritative source for metric derivations.
